decision_table.name: Determine_WA_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Washington B&O tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in Washington (office, employees, property)

condition.name: has_economic_nexus
condition.comment: Meets Washington economic nexus threshold ($100K or 200 transactions)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - B&O tax filing required // B&O tax will be calculated by table 51080

rule.policy:
Washington B&O tax filing required due to physical presence.
Physical presence includes: - Office or place of business in Washington - Employees working in Washington - Tangible property in Washington - Maintaining inventory in Washington - Regular solicitation in Washington
Reference: RCW 82.04.067 - Nexus Reference: WAC 458-20-193 - Interstate Sales Reference: WAC 458-20-19401 - Economic Nexus

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // B&O tax will be calculated by table 51080

rule.policy:
Washington B&O tax filing required due to economic nexus.
Economic nexus threshold (either): - $100,000 or more in Washington receipts (gross revenue), OR - 200 or more separate transactions in Washington
Washington adopted economic nexus following South Dakota v. Wayfair (2018).
Reference: RCW 82.04.067 - Economic Nexus Reference: WAC 458-20-19401 - Economic Nexus Rules Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018)
No Washington nexus - no B&O tax filing requirement. Any estimated payments would be refunded.

decision_table.name: Calculate_WA_Gross_Receipts
decision_table.description: Calculate Washington-sourced gross receipts for B&O tax. Uses apportionment to determine receipts attributable to Washington.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate WA gross receipts

condition.name: has_apportionment_percentage
condition.comment: Has calculated apportionment percentage to Washington

rule.policy:
Washington gross receipts calculation for B&O tax:
Washington uses market-based sourcing (destination) for most activities: - Sales of tangible property: destination of goods - Services: location where customer receives benefit - Intangibles/royalties: location of customer - Rental income: location of property
The B&O tax applies to gross receipts (revenue), not net income.
Reference: RCW 82.04.460 - Apportionment Reference: WAC 458-20-19402 - Single-Factor Receipts Apportionment Reference: WAC 458-20-14601 - Service and Other Activities

actions.action: // No apportionment calculated - assume 100% WA if nexus exists result.wa_gross_receipts = revenue.total_revenue;

rule.policy: No apportionment percentage calculated - treating all receipts as Washington-sourced. This is conservative approach when apportionment data is unavailable.
No Washington nexus - no gross receipts attributed to Washington.

decision_table.name: Determine_WA_Business_Classification
decision_table.description: Determine Washington business classification for B&O tax rate. Sets appropriate B&O tax rate based on primary business activity.

rule.policy:
Washington B&O tax - Retailing classification: 0.471%
Retailing includes sales of tangible personal property to consumers for consumption or use (not for resale).
Reference: RCW 82.04.250 - Retailing Reference: RCW 82.04.470 - Retailing B&O Tax Rate

Washington B&O tax - Wholesaling classification: 0.484%
Wholesaling includes sales of tangible personal property to persons for purpose of resale.
Reference: RCW 82.04.060 - Wholesaling Reference: RCW 82.04.270 - Wholesaling B&O Tax

Washington B&O tax - Manufacturing classification: 0.484%
Manufacturing includes production of articles for sale from raw materials, including processing, fabricating, assembling, extracting, and more.
Note: Certain manufacturers may qualify for preferential rates or exemptions.
Reference: RCW 82.04.240 - Manufacturing Reference: RCW 82.04.440 - Manufacturing B&O Tax

actions.action: // Financial Business B&O rate: 1.5% result.wa_bo_tax_rate = result.wa_financial_rate;

rule.policy:
Washington B&O tax - Financial Business classification: 1.5%
Financial business includes banks, savings and loan associations, credit unions, finance companies, insurance companies, and similar institutions.
This is the highest B&O tax rate classification.
Reference: RCW 82.04.290 - Financial Business

actions.action: // Professional Services B&O rate: 0.484% result.wa_bo_tax_rate = result.wa_professional_rate;

rule.policy:
Washington B&O tax - Professional Services classification: 0.484%
Professional services include legal, accounting, engineering, consulting, and other professional activities.
Reference: RCW 82.04.290 - Service and Other Activities

actions.action: // Service and Other Activities B&O rate: 0.484% result.wa_bo_tax_rate = result.wa_service_rate;

rule.policy:
Washington B&O tax - Service and Other Activities classification: 0.484%
This is the catch-all classification for business activities not specifically classified elsewhere.
Reference: RCW 82.04.290 - Service and Other Activities

decision_table.name: Calculate_WA_Small_Business_Credit
decision_table.description: Calculate Washington small business B&O tax credit. Available for businesses with gross revenue under $250K.

condition.name: below_small_business_threshold
condition.comment: Total revenue below $250K small business threshold

condition.name: has_wa_gross_receipts
condition.comment: Has Washington gross receipts subject to B&O tax

rule.policy:
Washington Small Business B&O Tax Credit:
Businesses with gross revenue under $250,000 qualify for a small business credit that reduces B&O tax liability. The credit amount phases out as revenue increases.
The credit is calculated on a monthly basis and varies based on: - Total gross revenue (all sources) - Type of business activity - Location (may vary for different jurisdictions)
Credit cannot exceed B&O tax liability (no refunds for excess credit).
Reference: RCW 82.04.4451 - Small Business B&O Credit Reference: WAC 458-20-104 - Small Business Tax Relief
No small business credit - gross revenue exceeds $250,000 threshold.
No small business credit - no Washington gross receipts to apply credit against.

decision_table.name: Calculate_WA_BO_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate Washington Business & Occupation (B&O) tax. Applies B&O tax rate to Washington-sourced gross receipts.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe B&O tax

rule.policy:
Washington Business & Occupation (B&O) Tax Calculation:
IMPORTANT: Washington has NO corporate income tax. The B&O tax is a gross receipts tax, NOT an income tax.
1. Washington gross receipts: [WA-sourced revenue] 2. Business classification: [service/retailing/wholesaling/manufacturing/financial] 3. B&O tax rate: [0.471%-1.5% depending on classification] 4. B&O tax before credits: = [Gross receipts × Rate] 5. Small business credit: - [Credit if revenue < $250K] 6. Other credits: - [High tech, aerospace, etc.] 7. B&O tax liability: = [Final tax]
Key Differences from Income Tax: - Based on GROSS RECEIPTS (revenue), not net income - No deductions for expenses, COGS, or payroll - Much lower rates (under 1.5%) but applies to gross revenue - Must be paid even if business operates at a loss
Reference: RCW 82.04 - Business and Occupation Tax Reference: WAC 458-20-104 - Small Business Tax Relief Reference: Form ETA - Combined Excise Tax Return Reference: Washington Department of Revenue Publication - B&O Tax Classification
No Washington nexus - no B&O tax liability. Any estimated payments are refunded.
No Washington gross receipts - no B&O tax liability. Filing may still be required to report no tax due.
